Advances: specled.mix_tasks, specled.prime, specled.next

From the pre-ship critical review, Tier-2 items U2/U7/U8/U13/U15/U16, all calibrated Medium or Low.

U2 — specled.tasks.verdict_line scope clause is circular as written ("for every pass and fail path WHERE THE TASK ITSELF REPORTS A VERDICT"). The covering scenario already enumerates six real paths and IS falsifiable; hoist that enumeration into the requirement statement and name the excluded pre-report raise paths explicitly. NOTE: the grammar has since gained tier=usage (specled_-0x4.2) and spec.validate's min-strength pre-flight now emits tier=usage too (specled_-wli) — hoist the enumeration as it exists NOW, not as the review snapshot described it.

U7 — verdict_line is UNDER-credited: the tier=branch form that motivated the whole epic has no test tagged to it. spec_check_test.exs:70 is tagged check_verbose_flag + branch_findings_breakdown; its verdict assertion is at :92. Add specled.tasks.verdict_line to the @tag spec: lists on the tier=branch, pass, spec.validate pass, argument-rejection and min-strength tests. NOTE: specled_-0x4.2 already added per-test verdict_line tags at spec_tasks_test.exs:589/:925/:946 (an auditor flagged that per-test @tag OVERWRITES @moduletag for the same key at ExUnit runtime, degrading per-test attribution — when adding ids to an already-tagged test, include the union you intend, not just the one id); the wli min-strength pin at spec_tasks_test.exs:935-944 is still untagged.

U8 — prime/next verdict_read_protocol are OVER-credited: tagged at @moduletag scope (spec_prime_task_test.exs:4-21), so every test in the module vouches for them and the two assertions that actually prove them could be deleted with the gate still green. Move the ids onto the specific tests. NOTE: specled_-0x4.1 added a golden test in spec_next_task_test.exs:27-30 tagged specled.next.verdict_read_protocol per-test; keep it credited.

U13 — drain_shell_messages/1 (test_support/specled_ex_case.ex:122-124; locate the actual path) matches {:mix_shell, _level, payload}, discarding the level, so "last stdout line" assertions actually prove "last shell message". Add a level-preserving drain_shell_events/0 and assert {:info, verdict} on one pass-path and one fail-path test; existing call sites keep working.

U15/U16 — no fixture pairs an info finding with an error, so the middle sort rank is unpinned (spec_check_test.exs:82 asserts info=0). Add an info-severity finding to the mixed fixture so all three ranks are ordered in one run, and replace the paired find_index comparisons with a severity-sequence partition assertion that stays correct as the fixture grows.

## Spec co-change authorization

Editing .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md, .spec/specs/prime.spec.md, .spec/specs/next.spec.md (the Advances: subjects) and .spec/realization_hashes.json (via documented regeneration) is IN SCOPE. Minimal prose-only reconciliation edits to OTHER subject specs are authorized ONLY when the spec gate demands them (branch_guard_missing_subject_update) — prove demand with a COMMITTED-revert probe (checkout-only reverts are vacuous; see epic LESSONS), keep to the smallest edit that keeps the gate green, and every file such a note names must genuinely be in your diff. This authorization comes before any scope warning below.

## Allowed touches

- test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs
- test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_task_test.exs
- test/mix/tasks/spec_next_task_test.exs
- test_support/** and test/support/** (whichever holds specled_ex_case.ex; test fixtures for U15 live wherever the mixed fixture is defined — follow the existing fixture mechanism)
- .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md
- .spec/specs/prime.spec.md
- .spec/specs/next.spec.md
- .spec/realization_hashes.json

## Out of Scope (files)

- lib/** — NO production code changes; U13 is test-support only
- docs/**, skills/**

## Out of Scope (intent)

- Do not weaken any requirement: U2 is a precision hoist, not a scope reduction — the six-path enumeration becomes requirement text and the excluded pre-report raise paths are named, nothing is dropped
- Do not reword the verdict read-protocol sentence or the verdict grammar
- No new deps
- Tag edits must never REDUCE the set of requirement ids a test vouches for (the @tag-overwrites-@moduletag trap)

## Verification

- mix spec.check --no-run-commands passes on the stage branch (test-tag consistency included)
- U7: the tier=branch, pass-path, spec.validate pass, argument-rejection and min-strength tests each carry specled.tasks.verdict_line (verify via the tag scanner or spec.check test-tag consistency, and confirm runtime tags with ExUnit metadata if practical)
- U8: prime/next verdict_read_protocol ids are credited ONLY by the tests that actually assert them; deleting either proving assertion now fails tagged_tests coverage or the test itself
- U13: drain_shell_events/0 exists in the shared case; at least one pass-path and one fail-path test assert {:info, <verdict>}; existing drain_shell_messages call sites unchanged
- U15/U16: one run orders error > warning > info in the mixed fixture; partition-style assertion replaces paired find_index comparisons
- Targeted: all four task test files green; mix format --check-formatted clean

Gaps:

1. The @tag-overwrites-@moduletag trap was walked into, in the one file where it bites. spec_tasks_test.exs carries a 22-id `@moduletag spec: [...]` that ALREADY includes specled.tasks.verdict_line (line 26). This branch added `@tag spec: ["specled.tasks.verdict_line"]` — a bare single-element list, not the union — to five tests in that module (:191, :258, :690, :911, :945). I confirmed ExUnit's merge semantics empirically with a standalone probe (`@moduletag spec: ["a","b","c"]` + `@tag spec: ["z"]` yields context[:spec] == ["z"]; an untagged sibling yields ["a","b","c"]). So each of those five tests' effective runtime attribution went from 22 ids to 1. This is exactly what the ticket's Out of Scope (intent) forbids — "Tag edits must never REDUCE the set of requirement ids a test vouches for (the @tag-overwrites-@moduletag trap)" — and exactly what U7's own NOTE warned about ("include the union you intend, not just the one id"). The reduction is substantive, not nominal: :690 "spec.check executes commands by default" genuinely exercises specled.tasks.check_strict_gate, and :191/:258 genuinely exercise specled.tasks.validate_exit_status / validate_findings; those ids' assertions live in those tests and the tests no longer vouch for them at runtime. This is also a CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE DELIVERABLE: the same implementer wrote the full moduletag union into the per-test tags in spec_prime_task_test.exs and spec_next_task_test.exs, so the methodology was understood and then not applied here; and the IMPLEMENTED comment claims U7 was done "without reducing existing per-test id sets", which is true only under a narrow reading (these five tests had no PRIOR per-test tag) and false for the set of ids each test vouches for. Gate impact is nil — lib/specled_ex/tag_scanner.ex unions module_ids into every test's id set (collect_moduletags/2 then process_statement/4), which is why `mix spec.check` stays green and why this needs a human/verifier to catch. Fix: expand each of the five per-test tags to the 22-id moduletag union plus specled.tasks.verdict_line, or leave those tests moduletag-only and rely on the scanner union.

2. New false credit on a test that asserts no verdict. spec_tasks_test.exs:911 "spec.check forwards min strength to strict verify" gained `@tag spec: ["specled.tasks.verdict_line"]` but its body (lines 911-934) contains zero `result=` assertions — it asserts `verification_strength_below_minimum` and refutes state.json, nothing more. Deleting `print_verdict/2` from spec.check's min-strength path would not fail this test. This is precisely the over-crediting pattern U8 exists to remove, re-introduced by U7 in the same commit — a second contradiction inside the deliverable. It is also unnecessary: spec.check's min-strength usage verdict is already proven and already tagged at spec_tasks_test.exs:957 ("spec.check rejects invalid min strength values", asserting `spec.check result=fail tier=usage error_findings=0`), and the min-strength pin the ticket actually named is :945. Fix: drop the tag at :911, or add the missing verdict assertion to that test.

3. Behavioral `then:` clauses in two scenarios were replaced by test-attribution bookkeeping. specled.prime.verdict_read_protocol.loop_text previously read `then: - The suggestion includes the verdict read protocol sentence.` It now reads `then: - The human-loop and JSON-loop tests that directly assert the suggestion includes the verdict read protocol sentence carry this requirement's per-test attribution.` That is now the scenario's ONLY then-clause, so the scenario for a `must` requirement no longer states any observable outcome of the system — it states what the test suite is tagged with, and is satisfiable by tagging alone. specled.next.verdict_read_protocol.commands got the same treatment (both then-clauses rewritten around "carries this requirement's per-test attribution"), though it at least retains the golden-assertion semantics. The requirement STATEMENTS are intact and unweakened, and no gate rule forbids this (append_only/scenario_regression did not fire), so this is the softest of the three gaps — but it is a spec-honesty regression in the same epic whose last main commit was the spec-honesty slice, and U8 asked only for tag moves, not scenario rewrites. Fix: restore the observable then-clause ("The suggestion includes the verdict read protocol sentence.") and, if per-test attribution is worth recording in the spec, add it as an additional clause rather than a replacement.

Notes (advisory only):
- The verdict grammar's alternatives list still enumerates only `spec.validate result=fail tier=validate error_findings=<N>` for spec.validate, while U2's new enumeration explicitly names spec.validate's min-strength pre-flight fail path — which emits `tier=usage` (spec.validate.ex validate_min_strength!, asserted at spec_tasks_test.exs:953). The generic "`tier=usage` identifies task-level pre-flight rejections" clause partially covers it. Pre-existing (wli introduced validate's tier=usage), not created here, but U2's hoist makes the omission more visible and this was the natural moment to fix it.
- Relatedly, spec.validate's argument-rejection path emits `tier=validate` (validate_args! defaults) while spec.check's emits `tier=usage`, which sits awkwardly against "tier=usage identifies task-level pre-flight rejections before validation starts". Pre-existing code behavior; worth a separate ticket.
- The probe methodology should be fixed for future stages: run committed-revert probes on a detached HEAD so no probe commits land on the stage branch at all. This branch's pair happens to net to zero, but it leaves two commits a reviewer must diff to trust.
- All probes I ran are fully unwound: git status clean, HEAD still 14d4068f55ffef999d39ff546d8f112834b83973, probe commit d9c62041 orphaned and unreachable from any branch.

The reduction is substantive: :690 is the sole proof that spec.check executes commands by default (asserts checked.txt at :714), :191 proves the validate fail exit path, :258 proves `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0`, and at runtime those tests now vouch for verdict_line only. Verifier output was sound; one immaterial slip: the spec_tasks_test.exs moduletag holds 23 ids (lines 5-27), not 22 — its "22-id union PLUS verdict_line" is numerically right since verdict_line sits at line 26. I found no missed instances: the only other tag edits in the diff are spec_check_test.exs:70 (2-id list expanded to 3, and that module's moduletag at :5 is the single id check_verbose_flag, which the list retains — no reduction), and spec_prime_task_test.exs:24/:98 plus spec_next_task_test.exs:31, which I checked id-by-id against their post-removal moduletags and which are exact unions plus the protocol id. The pre-existing bare tags at spec_tasks_test.exs:592, :618, :719, :934, :956, :967 are from specled_-0x4.2 and are NOT in this diff — leave them alone here. The only spec-scenario rewrites in the whole diff are the prime/next hunks; mix_tasks.spec.md changed only the U2 requirement statement and evidence_store.spec.md only its prose note.

Bounce reason:

1. spec_tasks_test.exs:191, :258, :690, :945 — DELETE the four added `@tag spec: ["specled.tasks.verdict_line"]` lines outright. Removal is preferred over expansion and loses nothing: verdict_line is already in the module's 23-id @moduletag, so tag_scanner.ex:189 still attributes it statically AND the tests regain their full 23-id runtime attribution — strictly better than the bare tag on both axes. Deleting them returns those four tests to their base (f3f2d845) tag state, which was gate-green, so this cannot regress test-tag consistency. U7's verification bullet is still met: each of those tests carries verdict_line via the moduletag. If you nonetheless want explicit per-test credit, the ONLY acceptable alternative is the full 23-id moduletag union written out verbatim (verdict_line included) — a bare or partial list is forbidden by Out of Scope (intent).

2. spec_tasks_test.exs:911 — DROP the tag (do not add an assertion). The min-strength verdict is already proven at :957. Be aware this restores base state rather than fully de-crediting :911, because the 23-id moduletag blankets the whole module; that broad-brush moduletag over-credit is pre-existing and out of this ticket's remit — do not attempt to fix it here.

3. Scenarios — RESTORE the observable then-clauses verbatim from f3f2d845. prime.spec.md specled.prime.verdict_read_protocol.loop_text must read `- The suggestion includes the verdict read protocol sentence.` next.spec.md specled.next.verdict_read_protocol.commands must read `- The commands section also includes the verdict read protocol sentence.` and `- A direct golden assertion compares the shared helper output with the full literal sentence, so future wording changes require an intentional test update.` Per-test attribution bookkeeping may be ADDED as an extra then-clause but must never replace an observable outcome.
